candidates.label: location

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". candidates.label: events

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation

Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". candidates.label: recordedAt

Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: deathPlace

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: startTime

candidates.label: duration

candidates.label: source

candidates.label: affiliation

candidates.label: relatedTherapy

candidates.label: warning

candidates.label: issuedBy

candidates.label: alcoholWarning

Examples: "A medication's alcohol warning states 'Do not consume alcohol'.", "The drug's alcohol warning advises 'Limit alcohol intake'."

candidates.label: reviewedBy

candidates.label: legislationChanges
candidates.comment: A legislative alteration relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it modifies, replaces, corrects, or repeals. Also called alters law, modifies statute, replaces act, repeals legislation. Examples: Legislation X legislationChanges 'Legislation Y'. The new regulation legislationChanges 'several existing laws'. This amendment legislationChanges 'the previous version of the act'. Distinct from legislationAmends, which is a specific type of change (introducing legal changes), and legislationConsolidates, which is about creating a consolidated version.

candidates.label: isAccessoryOrSparePartFor
candidates.comment: A product compatibility relation between a product and the other products for which it serves as an accessory or spare part. Also called accessory for, spare part for, compatible with, used with. Examples: A phone case isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'iPhone 15'. A replacement battery isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'Laptop Model X'. A camera lens isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'DSLR Camera Y'. Distinct from isConsumableFor, which refers to items that are used up.

candidates.label: replacee
candidates.comment: A replacee relation between a replace action and the entity that is being substituted. Also called item replaced, old item. Examples: "A replace action involves a replacee 'old battery'.", "A document update replaces 'version 1.0'.", "A software upgrade replaces 'legacy system'.". Distinct from replacer, which is the entity doing the replacing.

candidates.label: replacer
candidates.comment: A replacer relation between a replace action and the entity that performs the substitution. Also called new item, replacement item. Examples: "A replace action involves a replacer 'new battery'.", "A document update uses a replacer 'version 2.0'.", "A software upgrade uses a replacer 'modern system'.". Distinct from replacee, which is the entity being replaced.

candidates.label: isAccessoryOrSparePartFor
candidates.comment: A product compatibility relation between a product and the other products for which it serves as an accessory or spare part. Also called accessory for, spare part for, compatible with, used with. Examples: A phone case isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'iPhone 15'. A replacement battery isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'Laptop Model X'. A camera lens isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'DSLR Camera Y'. Distinct from isConsumableFor, which refers to items that are used up.

candidates.label: option
candidates.comment: A text or thing representing an option available for a choose action. Also called choice, alternative, selection. Examples: "Choose Meal Action option 'Chicken'", "Choose Color Action option 'Blue'", "Choose Destination Action option 'Paris'". Distinct from object, which is the general item acted upon.

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: availableFrom
candidates.comment: A date and time when an item is available for pickup from a store or locker. Also called: pickup start time, ready for collection. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableFrom '2023-10-27T10:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableFrom '2023-10-28'". Distinct from availableThrough, which specifies the end of pickup availability.

candidates.label: addOn
candidates.comment: An add-on relation between a base offer and an additional offer that can only be acquired in conjunction with it. Also called supplementary offer, bundled offer, extra option. Examples: "A car purchase offer has an add-on for extended warranty.", "A software license offer has an add-on for premium support."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."
